title: Analytic: optical parametric amplification, cosh^2 signal gain (nonlinear FDFD)
description:
Non-degenerate parametric gain (em_fdfd_nonlinear, coupling_mode pump_depleted, Newton-Krylov): a y-periodic strip (4 rows of 10 nm, CPML along x) filled everywhere, PML included, with a birefringent medium: the H_z pump p (800 nm, E_y along x) sees eps_yy = eps_p, the E_z signal s (1300 nm) and the generated E_z idler i = p - s (2080 nm) see eps_zz = 2.25; eps_p is chosen so that the three 3-point lattice waves are exactly phase matched, K_p = K_s + K_i per cell (eps_p = 2.2482). A 20 um chi2 slab (chi2_medium, crystal_class general, d23 = d34 = 25 pm/V) couples them: P_z(s) = 2 eps0 d E_y(p) conj(E_z(i)), P_z(i) = 2 eps0 d E_y(p) conj(E_z(s)) (the conjugated slots of the DFG terms). Line sources launch the pump (amplitude A_p, set from the gain length product gL) and a weak signal A_s = 1e-3 A_p (no pump depletion). The sweep runs gL over 0.25-2.
Analytic (lattice coupled-mode theory): with kappa_s,i = k_s,i^2 d h / sin(K_s,i h), g L = |E_p| L sqrt(kappa_s kappa_i), |E_p| the pump at the cell centres (A_p cos(K_p h / 2)); the signal power gain is cosh^2(g L) and the idler conversion (|E_i| / A_s)^2 kappa_s / kappa_i = sinh^2(g L) (gain 2.38 at g L = 1, 14.1 at 2).
Sweep tab: G_signal and G_idler vs gL with the dashed cosh^2 / sinh^2 curves (log axis helps).
Derived values tab: G_signal, G_idler and E_pump (the undepleted pump beyond the slab) against their references; expected ~1-2 % (coupled-mode accuracy and the backward waves; to be confirmed by a first run).
